body:
Slice 6 of 6 of #508. Depends on #655 (the `MAX_MAP_CHUNKS` constants); independent of the multipart verbs.

## What

0016 decision 7's wire half for ordinary PUTs — segmentation is multipart-only, so `PutObject` stays flat and reaches large sizes by chunk-size selection: `chunk_size_effective = max(DEFAULT_CHUNK_SIZE, ceil(Content-Length / MAX_MAP_CHUNKS))`; refused `400 EntityTooLarge` when it cannot fit `MAX_MAP_CHUNKS` even at `chunk_size_max`; a lengthless `aws-chunked` stream (which cannot evaluate the formula — `x-amz-decoded-content-length` is optional) uses the size-independent `ceil(5 GiB / MAX_MAP_CHUNKS)`, with the configuration precondition `chunk_size_max >= ceil(5 GiB / MAX_MAP_CHUNKS)` checked at configuration load and a header-time refusal — never a mid-stream failure — when a deployment does not meet it.

## Acceptance

- a declared-length PUT past the flat ceiling publishes a map of <= `MAX_MAP_CHUNKS` chunks; one that cannot fit even at `chunk_size_max` is refused EntityTooLarge at header time; today's lengthless streaming PUT keeps working; the config precondition is enforced at load;
- `cargo xtask ci` green.

Part of #508 / epic #513.
